source_title: Carragher apologises to Villa for 'wrong' language
source_excerpt:
Former Liverpool defender Carragher works as a pundit for Sky Sports and American broadcaster CBS
Jamie Carragher has apologised to Aston Villa , the club's owners and their fans for using "clumsy and wrong" language when linking manager Unai Emery with becoming Manchester United head coach.
On Friday, Villa said they would initiate legal action against the former England defender for what they described as "unacceptable insults".
The club's statement, signed by chairman Nassef Sawiris, referred to comments made by Carragher on the Stick to Football podcast, when he suggested Emery would want to manage a "giant" club.
He also told the club's fans to shut up, adding: " Aston Villa will never be Manchester United ."
Posting on social media on Saturday, Carragher said his comments were intended to be "tongue in cheek".
"I'd like to apologise to Aston Villa , the owners and their fans," the pundit wrote.
"My language this week was clumsy and wrong.
"I can assure Villa fans it was tongue in cheek but I can understand it's not come across that way, so apologies."
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick's position is hanging in the balance following a dismal start to the season.
Referring to former Paris St-Germain and Arsenal boss Emery, Carragher said on Stick to Football: "Surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again.
"There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.
"So Real Madrid will take Manchester United 's best player, they did it with [Cristiano] Ronaldo. And there will be teams below Aston Villa , and they'll take their players or manager, so shut the [expletive] up Aston Villa fans. Aston Villa will never be Manchester United ."
After his comments attracted criticism from Villa fans, Carragher responded on social media, stating that telling them to shut up had been "a joke" and he had been praising Emery and the club "for years".
He reiterated on the Overlap Daily podcast that his message to Villa fans had been meant "in jest", adding: "I just think Unai Emery is the best manager in the league and if you're Man Utd you're thinking, what's the best we can get?"

## जेमी कैरेगर का माफीनामा

पूर्व लिवरपूल डिफेंडर और फुटबॉल पंडित जेमी कैरेगर ने एस्टन विला क्लब, उसके मालिकों और प्रशंसकों से अपनी टिप्पणियों के लिए माफी मांग ली है। रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, उन्होंने स्वीकार किया है कि एस्टन विला के मैनेजर उनाई एम्री को मैनचेस्टर यूनाइटेड से जोड़ने के दौरान उनके द्वारा इस्तेमाल की गई भाषा "बेढंगी और गलत" थी।

## विवाद की पृष्ठभूमि

यह विवाद तब शुरू हुआ जब 'स्टिक टू फुटबॉल' पॉडकास्ट पर चर्चा के दौरान कैरेगर ने सुझाव दिया था कि उनाई एम्री किसी "विशाल" क्लब का प्रबंधन करना चाहेंगे। अपनी बात को आगे बढ़ाते हुए उन्होंने विला प्रशंसकों से जुड़ी कुछ ऐसी बातें कहीं, जिन्हें क्लब ने "अस्वीकार्य अपमान" करार दिया।

रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, शुक्रवार को एस्टन विला ने कहा था कि वे पूर्व इंग्लैंड डिफेंडर के खिलाफ कानूनी कार्रवाई शुरू करेंगे। इस संबंध में क्लब के चेयरमैन नासेफ सॉइरिस के हस्ताक्षर से एक आधिकारिक बयान भी जारी किया गया था।

## स्पष्टीकरण और प्रतिक्रिया

शनिवार को सोशल मीडिया पर एक पोस्ट के माध्यम से कैरेगर ने स्पष्ट किया कि उनकी टिप्पणियां "मजाकिया लहजे" (tongue in cheek) में थीं। उन्होंने लिखा:

* "मैं एस्टन विला, मालिकों और उनके प्रशंसकों से माफी मांगना चाहता हूँ।"
* "इस सप्ताह मेरी भाषा बेढंगी और गलत थी।"
* "मैं विला प्रशंसकों को आश्वस्त कर सकता हूँ कि यह बात मजाक में कही गई थी, लेकिन मैं समझ सकता हूँ कि यह उस रूप में सामने नहीं आई, इसलिए मैं माफी मांगता हूँ।"

बाद में 'द ओवरलैप डेली' पॉडकास्ट पर भी उन्होंने दोहराया कि उनका संदेश हंसी-मजाक में था और उनका इरादा उनाई एम्री तथा क्लब की प्रशंसा करने का था।

## आगे की स्थिति और सत्यापन

* **पुष्ट जानकारी:** कैरेगर द्वारा सोशल मीडिया पर सार्वजनिक रूप से माफी मांग ली गई है और एस्टन विला ने कानूनी कार्रवाई की बात कही थी।
* **रिपोर्ट किए गए दावे:** पॉडकास्ट के दौरान दिए गए बयान और क्लब की ओर से जारी बयान।
* **अज्ञात तथ्य:** इस मामले में आगे की कानूनी प्रक्रिया या क्लब की अंतिम प्रतिक्रिया क्या होगी, इसकी पूरी जानकारी अभी सामने नहीं आई है।

पाठक इस घटना से जुड़ी आधिकारिक घोषणाओं और क्लब के बयानों को एस्टन विला के आधिकारिक सोशल मीडिया हैंडल या सत्यापित खेल समाचार पोर्टल्स के माध्यम से सत्यापित कर सकते हैं।

en_body:
## Pundit Apologizes After Aston Villa Threatens Legal Action

Former Liverpool defender and television pundit Jamie Carragher has issued a public apology to Aston Villa, the club's owners, and their supporters following remarks he made regarding manager Unai Emery and Manchester United. 

The controversy arose after comments made by Carragher on the *Stick to Football* podcast. During the broadcast, the pundit discussed the managerial hierarchy in football and suggested that Emery would likely want the opportunity to manage Manchester United, describing them as a "giant" club. He also made remarks telling Aston Villa fans to "shut up" and stated that "Aston Villa will never be Manchester United."

## Club Response and Legal Threat

In response to the podcast appearance, Aston Villa released a strong statement on Friday signed by chairman Nassef Sawiris. The club announced that they would initiate legal action against Carragher for what they characterized as "unacceptable insults."

## Clarification and Apology

Following the backlash and the club's legal warning, Carragher took to social media on Saturday to clarify his remarks and offer an apology.

* "I'd like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners and their fans," Carragher wrote online.
* He stated that his language had been "clumsy and wrong."
* He assured supporters that his remarks were intended to be "tongue in cheek" and "a joke," though he acknowledged that they did not come across that way.

Carragher later reiterated on *The Overlap Daily* podcast that his intention was to praise Emery, whom he described as "the best manager in the league," while discussing potential managerial options for Manchester United.

## Practical Implications and Verification

For sports followers seeking to verify the original announcements and statements:
* Review official statements published directly through Aston Villa's official club communication channels.
* Listen to the referenced episodes of the *Stick to Football* and *The Overlap Daily* podcasts for the complete context of the initial remarks.
* Check official social media profiles of the involved commentators and broadcasters for direct statements.
